annotation.title_clean: Artificial Intelligence in Policing: Research report 2 – AI technologies currently used to improve the efficiency and service delivery of police's corporate or enabling functions
annotation.title_en: Artificial Intelligence in Policing: Research report 2 – AI technologies currently used to improve the efficiency and service delivery of police's corporate or enabling functions
annotation.authors_or_issuer: New Zealand Police, Evidence Based Policing Centre
named_instruments_referenced: EU Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI
annotation.summary_en: This is the second of four New Zealand Police Evidence Based Policing Centre research reports, published July 2024. It reviews AI tools that police use for corporate and enabling functions, such as documentation, audio and video analysis, data integration, biometrics, call management, community interaction and recruitment. It identifies problems with performance, integration, governance, privacy and staff trust, and recommends keeping a human in the loop.
key_provisions_or_claims: AI can speed up repetitive tasks such as documentation, redaction, transcription and data integration in policing.
Biased algorithms, poor data and AI's inability to understand context lead to inaccurate results.
A human must stay in the loop, supported by training and ongoing oversight.
Effective integration, governance and data architecture are needed, which may mean re-engineering workflows.
Staff trust in AI is weakened by fears of deskilling and job losses, which calls for open communication.
